analytic.title: Schedulability of Strictly Periodic Tasks with Communication Dependence

application.desc: GROBID - A machine learning software for extracting information from scholarly documents

div.p: Non-preemptive tasks with strict periods are usually adopted in practical multi-core real-time systems when continual sampling and processing of data are required. Systems designers need to provide a proper scheduling strategy such that the tasks deadlines will be met even under the worst-case conditions. In this paper, we study the scheduling problem of non-preemptive tasks with strict periods in multi-core real-time systems. First, we analyze the characteristics of the multi-core real-time system, build a task model with strict periodic constraints, analyze the requirements of space resources, time resources and communication delay when the system can be scheduled, and propose a solution to determine the task schedulability based on mixed integer linear programming. The practical results show that the proposed solution can not only be used to determine the schedulability of multi-core real-time system, but also to obtain the minimum number of processors needed by the system, which can guide the design of the system.

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: With the rapid development of microelectronics and computer technology, the structure and function of real-time system is becoming more and more complex. Its design is also developing towards integration, modularization, generalization and intelligence. Multi-core architecture [1] has been widely used to meet the increasing performance requirements of realtime system. Multi core processors can perform more tasks in a specific clock cycle. Multi-core architecture can make software run better and create a more perfect architecture for future software writing [2]. Multi-core technology can make servers process tasks in parallel, and use less power in computing power consumption and generate less heat [3].

Therefore, to ensure the correctness of multi-core real-time system, its correctness depends not only on the logical results of system calculation, but also on the response time of system processing. When generating external events or data, the realtime system must be able to accept and respond quickly within the specified time [4]. In order to accurately manage time resources, improve the design and implementation efficiency of multi-core real-time system, and ensure that the system design meets the requirements of real-time and predictability, it is necessary to determine the schedulability of different task sets [5]. The scheduling algorithm checks the time constraints of system tasks, provides appropriate scheduling for task execution, and significantly improves the design and implementation efficiency of multi-core real-time system [6]. However, it is difficult to find a good scheduling algorithm, not only because the non preemptive attribute makes the task scheduling NP complex, but also because of strict cycle constraints, it is difficult to adjust the judgment conditions of scheduling [7].

At present, the system needs to support more complex applications, and complex application tasks often contain complex dependencies, and with the significant increase in the number of tasks, it becomes more complex to find a good scheduling algorithm [8]. This paper analyzes the characteristics of communication correlation, establishes a task model with strict cycle constraints, describes schedulable space constraints, time constraints and communication delay constraints. Based on mixed integer linear programming (MILP) [9], a strict cyclic task scheduling scheme with communication dependence is proposed. This scheme can not only judge the schedulability of the system [10], but also allocate appropriate hardware resources and time resources for each task, so as to obtain the minimum number of processors needed by the system and guide the design of the whole system [11].

div.head: II. RELATE WORK
div.p: In the field of real-time scheduling, there have been many works studying the allocation and scheduling of strictly periodic tasks. For example, in AlSheikh et al. the authors first used the Mixed Integer Linear Program (MILP) formulation to build an exact framework for the non-preemptive periodic scheduling problem in Integrated Modular Avionics (IMA) platform where all avionic tasks were real-time and under strict periodicity constraint [12]. Then, they presented a best response algorithm based on the game theoretic approach to calculate the largest possible change for the execution times of all tasks. Finally, the authors used the common scaling factor to determine whether or not [13].

Based on the work of Al-Sheikh et al., Pira and Artigues presented a new method to compute the best response and improved the original algorithm with local optimizations and a propagation mechanism [14].Periodic tasks with communication dependence are also studied. Julien Forget propose fixed priority scheduling policies for different classes of dependent tasks:with simultaneous or arbitrary release times, with simple precedences (between tasks of the same period) or extended precedences (between tasks of different periods).

Strict periodic tasks with communication dependence have not been studied.Through the analysis of communication depends on the characteristic of the system is constructed with strict cycle constraints task model, describes the system schedulable space constraints, time constraints, and the communication time delay constraint, and based on Mixed Integer Linear Programming (Mixed Integer Linear Programming, MILP),put forward with communication depend on strict cycle task scheduling solution of sex determination.

div.head: III. MODEL
div.p: In this paper, we consider a real-time system composed of m processor π = π 1 , π 2 , ..., π m and n task θ = θ 1 , θ 2 , ..., θ n . Each processor π k (k ∈ [1, m]) in the system has a fixed free storage space M k and a maximum number of tasks N k that can be supported. At the same time, a two-dimensional array ⃗ λ = (λ k,l )(k, l ∈ [1, m]) of row m and column m is established to represent the communication delay between processors. Each element λ k,l is a floating-point value, indicating the maximum delay of data transmission between processor π k and processor π l . When k = l, λ k,l represents the internal communication delay of the processor [15].
Each task θ i (i ∈ [1, n]) in the system can be represented by a triple
div.formula: θ i = ⟨c i , p i , m i ⟩(i ∈ [1, n])
div.p: , where c i , p i , m i respectively represent the worst execution time,cycle and required storage space of task θ i .
For task θ i , if the start execution time is s i , the start running time of the r job is s i + rp i , and the end time is s i + rp i + c i , that is, the job runs in the time interval
div.formula: [s i + rp i , s i + rp i + c i ] [16]. Let B r i (s i ) represent the time occupied by the r operation of θ i , then B r i (s i ) = [s i + rp i , s i + rp i + c i ].

div.p: There will be data communication between different tasks,the two-dimensional array ⃗ ρ of n rows and n columns is used to represent the time of information transmission between tasks,and there will be a predetermined maximum communication delay between tasks to describe the time limit of data transmission between two tasks. The two-dimensional array ⃗ δ = (δ i,j )(i, j ∈ [1, n]) of row n and column n is used to represent the maximum communication delay of the task. Each element δ i,j is a floating-point value, indicating the maximum available time after the data is sent from task θ i and before it is received by task θ j .
IV. SCHEDULABILITY ANALYSIS When the real-time system is schedulable, all periodic tasks and processors in the system need to meet the constraints of space, time and communication delay.

1) Spatial constraints: (C1) each periodic task can and can only run on one processor; (C2) periodic tasks with mutual exclusion cannot run on the same processor; (C3) the number of periodic tasks running on each processor cannot exceed the maximum number it supports; (C4) the total storage space required for all periodic tasks running on each processor cannot exceed this Free storage space for the processor.

2) Time constraint: (C5) the first task of each cycle task must be completed before the end of the cycle task cycle; (C6) any two cycle tasks assigned to the same processor have no conflict in time [17].
3) Communication delay constraint: (C7) the data transfer time between any two periodic tasks cannot exceed the predefined maximum communication delay of these two periodic tasks.

When the set of periodic tasks is schedulable on the processor, each periodic task must be assigned a suitable processor and an effective start time to ensure that the whole real-time system meets the above three constraints.

div.head: C. Analysis of communication delay constraint

div.p: V. MILP SOLUTION MILP is used to judge the schedulability of the system. In the actual solution process, there may be multiple allocation methods that can meet all constraints. These allocation methods can ensure the schedulability of tasks. In order to achieve better system performance, an optimization goal is often proposed in the process of planning and solving to ensure the best operation of the system. The most commonly used strategy is to concentrate tasks as much as possible, get the minimum number of processors required by tasks, and save system weight and energy consumption.

div.head: VI. CASE ANALYSIS
div.p: In this section, a case study is used to illustrate the process of solving the schedulability problem of multi-core real-time system by MILP. There are five tasks in the system, and the parameters of each task are shown in Figure 3. Among them, task 1 needs to receive the control commands of other partitions within 300ms, while task 5 needs to receive the status information of other tasks within 400msThere is no communication time limit between other partitions. At the same time, task 1 and task 5 cannot run on the same processor. There are three isomorphic processors in the system, each of which has 10MB of free memory and three maximum tasks. The maximum communication delay between any two processors is 1ms. Using the model of the solution, the parameters of the system are described as follows:

( Bring the above processor parameters and task parameters into the MILP scheme, and use the CPLEX optimizer programming parser to solve them, and get the minimum number of processing modules m ′ = 2, partition offset -→ s = [0, 0, 1, 5, 3].tasks θ 2 and θ 5 are assigned on processor π 1 , while tasks θ 1 , θ 3 , θ 4 are assigned on processor π 2 . Because the whole task set only needs two processors,the system can be scheduled. According to the task offset vector -→ s and task ownership vector ⃗ a obtained by the MILP scheme, the main time frame on processors π 1 and π 2 is shown in Fig. 4. Based on the strict periodic tasks, this paper establishes the task model and processor model, analyzes the requirements of the communication dependent task system on space, time and communication delay, establishes the schedulability constraints, and searches all available solution spaces by using the mixed integer linear programming to obtain the solution of the system schedulability determination method. The solution proposed in this paper can not only determine the schedulability of the system, but also get the minimum number of processors required by the task set, reduce the weight and energy consumption of the system to the maximum extent, and provide a means for the allocation of system resources.

The possible direction of our future work: Considering the solution of multi task scheduling for multiprocessor platform with communication dependency without using MILP, and the results of this paper are extended to non strict periodic task scheduling.
